sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Garun Pal Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1-Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

2-By means of above application no. 30556 of 2024 under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Kuldeep who is involved in Case Crime No. 84 of 2024, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 307 and 34 I.P.C.,
Police Station Kotwali Chandpa, District Hathras seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
3-The prosecution case, in brief, is that in the night of 09.04.2024, the informant along with his brother Tinku and one Manish Sharma of his village were carrying chaff on his plot.
At around 11:52 p.m., Mohit and Kuldeep came there and said to get out of the road.

They also started abusing and Kuldeep vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163843632/
1 on making resistance, they slapped the informant and started assaulting him with kicks and fists and also fired upon him with an intention to kill.
They while leaving, threatened to kill him and fled.

4-The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that though the first information report has been lodged against Mohit and Kuldeep (present applicant) but in the impugned F.I.R., role of causing fire arm injury has not been specified.

Referring the injury report and supplementary report dated 10.04.2024 and 24.05.2024 of the informant/injured, it is submitted that the injury no.1, which is assigned to the applicant after F.I.R. is simple in nature,
therefore, applicant who is languishing in jail since 07.06.2024 is entitled to be released on bail.

So far as the criminal history of the applicant is concerned, it is submitted that the applicant has criminal history of one case, being case crime no. 35 of 2020 under Sections 376, 323 and 506 I.P.C.
registered at Police Station Chandpa, District Hathras, in which final report has been submitted.
5-Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that F.I.R. is not encyclopedia of every minute detail.
The prosecution case is corroborated from the medical examination report of the injured.

As per the statement of the informant, role of causing injury on his head with danda and iron bar has been assigned to the present applicant-Kuldeep,
hence, considering the gravity of the offence and criminal history of the applicant, the bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.
6-Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that the injured-Nizamuddin, in his statement recorded during investigation while supporting the prosecution case, also specified the role of the accused Mohit and Kuldeep stating inter-alia that Mohit Kumar had fired at him from gun, he also abused and threatened him to kill.
Kuldeep while abusing and threatening to kill hit him on his head with stick and iron bar which he was holding in his hand.
As per medical examination report of the injured, he has received two injuries.

Though the injury no.1 is simple in nature but the same has been found to be caused by hard and blunt object on the left parietal region above to left year, which is vital part of the body of the injured.

The injury no.
2 has been found to be caused by gunshot with a close range at upper part of middle and right thoracic region, right shoulder region and anterior part of neck, etc.
This Court is of the view that statement of the injured witness, which is corroborated from medical evidence can not be lightly brushed aside at this stage.
Investigating officer during investigation has also recorded the statement of independent eye witnesses, who have supported the prosecution case.
The bail application of co-accused Mohit has been rejected by this Court.
7-Considering the gravity of offence, role assigned to the applicant as noted above and severity of punishment, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
8-Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.
9-It is made clear that any observation made in this order is for the purpose of disposal of bail application and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

10-However, Superintendent of Police, Hathras is directed to ensure the production of all the remaining prosecution witnesses on the dates fixed before the trial court so that the trial of the applicant may be concluded at earliest.

11-On appearance of the prosecution witnesses, their statement shall be recorded on the same day without granting any adjournment to either of the parties.
12-Copy of this order be communicated to Superintendent of Police, Hathras as well as concerned trial court within two weeks for necessary information and compliance.
